data.title: Frontend
data.tagline: The layer people directly see, click, and type into
data.description: On a sign-up page, the fields, submit button, and pending, success, or error messages belong to the frontend; whether the account was actually created must come from the backend result.

flowLesson.title: Which parts handle one save?

steps.label: Edit and save
steps.detail: Read the input and show a pending state

steps.label: Send the request
steps.detail: Use the API contract's URL, method, and data

steps.label: Receive, check, and process
steps.detail: Receive the request and validate the input, identity, and permission

steps.label: Return the result
steps.detail: Return success, failure, and the reason under the API contract

steps.label: Show the result
steps.detail: Update the page from the real response

flowLesson.boundary: Frontend code runs in the browser, where visitors can inspect or modify it. Do not keep secrets, trusted prices, or permission rules only there.

practice.title: The page says Saved, but the old value returns after refresh. What should you check first?

options.label: Compare the save request, when success appears, and the response used after refresh
options.feedback: Correct. Together these show whether the UI reported success early and what refresh actually read.

options.label: Clear the browser cache first, then refresh and see whether the old value remains
options.feedback: Cache can affect display, but it does not prove the save completed or identify what refresh read.

options.label: Delay the success message by one second, then repeat save and refresh
options.feedback: Changing message timing does not fix a failed request, early success, or a read of the wrong record.

flowLesson.agentPrompt: The page says Saved, but the value disappears after refresh. Check whether the frontend reports success too early and whether it handles the save request and refresh read correctly. Fix the cause, then save and refresh again to verify it.
